title: The Grand Duchy Loop, Éislek Ridges to Moselle Terraces

bestPeriod.note: Late September puts the Moselle harvest and the Éislek beech colour in the same week.

summary: A 620 km loop of a country you can cross in ninety minutes, slate ridges, castle valleys, riverside vineyards and blast-furnace towns.
hook: Luxembourg is 82 km top to bottom, which is exactly why it rewards a slow week. The distances are trivial; the transitions are not. In four days you go from wind-scoured Ardennes plateau to Riesling terraces to the rust-red slag hills of the Minett, and each landscape has its own road manners.

snapshot.Country: Luxembourg, with short hops into Belgium and Germany
snapshot.Base(s): Clervaux (1 night), Vianden (2), Echternach (2), Luxembourg City (2)
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: approx. 620 km; plateau ridge roads, tight river-valley CRs, one motorway spine
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Luxembourg-Findel (LUX); rental desks in the terminal, 8 km from the city
snapshot.Who It Suits: Drivers who prefer 100 km of good road to 400 km of any road; castle and industrial-heritage people

itinerary.title: Off the A7 and onto the ridge
itinerary.morning: Collect the car at Findel and take the A7 *Nordstrooss* north, 30 km of new motorway that dives through the Grouft and Stafelter tunnels and spits you out at Schieren. It is free, like every road in Luxembourg.
itinerary.afternoon: At Ettelbruck join the N7, the Éislek ridge road: a long, exposed run over the Oesling plateau through Hoscheid and Marnach with big-sky views either side and a few 8% dips into stream valleys. Pull into the crest layby above Hoscheid for the first proper look north.
itinerary.evening: Clervaux, 78 km from the airport. Walk up to the château for *The Family of Man*, Edward Steichen's 1955 photographic exhibition, permanently installed here and inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World register.
itinerary.dayStats: 78 km · 1 h 15 drive · no passes, one plateau crest · max altitude 510 m at Hoscheid

itinerary.title: The Upper Sûre and the fuel-price border
itinerary.morning: West on the CR324 and N15 to the Upper Sûre lake (*Stauséi*). Park at the Burfelt viewpoint above Insenborn for the aerial view of the flooded valley, then drive the shoreline loop through Lultzhausen and Bavigne, narrow two-lane CRs with blind crests and constant cyclists.
itinerary.afternoon: Cross into Belgium at Martelange, where the N4 through the village is a wall of filling stations. Fuel is cheaper on the Luxembourg side of that strip than anywhere in Belgium, France or Germany, because Luxembourg's excise duty is lower. Return via Boulaide and Esch-sur-Sûre, where the road tunnels through solid rock into a village wrapped in a meander.
itinerary.evening: Drop south-east to Vianden via Wiltz on the N26 and CR322. The château sits floodlit above the Our; the village has one main street and a chairlift.
itinerary.dayStats: 118 km · 2 h 20 drive · no passes · max altitude 545 m near Bavigne

itinerary.title: Our valley, pumped storage and the castle road
itinerary.morning: Ride the Vianden chairlift for the castle-from-above view, then drive the hairpin road up to Mont Saint-Nicolas, upper reservoir of the SEO pumped-storage plant, a 1960s engineering set-piece with a gallery inside the mountain and a lake on the summit.
itinerary.afternoon: Take the CR324 north along the Our to Stolzembourg and Dasbourg, a slow shaded frontier road where the German bank is fifteen metres away. Turn back south for Bourscheid castle on its spur 150 m above the Sûre; the approach from Bourscheid-Moulin is a 12% climb with tight switchbacks.
itinerary.evening: Diekirch for the National Museum of Military History, the Ardennes offensive told through vehicles and dioramas, then back to Vianden.
itinerary.dayStats: 96 km · 2 h 05 drive · no passes · max altitude 505 m at Mont Saint-Nicolas

itinerary.title: Into the Mullerthal sandstone
itinerary.morning: East to Beaufort, where two castles share one site: the medieval ruin and the Renaissance château, which has produced blackcurrant liqueur for generations and pours tastings in the afternoon.
itinerary.afternoon: The CR121 to Berdorf, then a twenty-minute walk to the Schiessentümpel, the triple-arched waterfall on every poster of "Little Switzerland". The lane down to Echternach through the sandstone defile is genuinely narrow, with laybys used as passing places.
itinerary.evening: Echternach: the Basilica of St Willibrord, the abbey square and the lake on the edge of town. Use the Parking Charly car park rather than the old-town squares.
itinerary.dayStats: 74 km · 1 h 45 drive · no passes · max altitude 415 m near Berdorf

itinerary.title: The Route du Vin
itinerary.morning: Follow the Sûre down to Wasserbillig, then south on the N10, the Moselle wine road. Grevenmacher first: the Bernard-Massard cellars have made bottle-fermented Crémant de Luxembourg since 1921 and run guided tours with a tasting.
itinerary.afternoon: Machtum, Ahn and Wormeldange, where vineyards climb off the road at an alarming angle. The Musée du Vin at Ehnen is small and unfashionable and explains the terroir better than any tasting room. End at Remich and the Caves St Martin galleries cut into the rock.
itinerary.evening: Schengen, 8 km on, for the European Museum by the bridge. If you plan to taste properly, leave the car in Remich: all buses, trams and second-class trains nationwide are free for everyone, with no ticket at all.
itinerary.dayStats: 82 km · 1 h 50 drive · no passes · max altitude 320 m above Wormeldange

itinerary.title: The Minett: iron, slag and reclaimed ground
itinerary.morning: South-west on the free A13 to Fond-de-Gras, a preserved industrial site where the Train 1900 steam service and the narrow-gauge *Minièresbunn* mine railway both run on summer weekends. Check operating days first.
itinerary.afternoon: Rumelange's National Mine Museum takes you into the gallery by mine train, 12°C underground, year-round. Then Esch-sur-Alzette and Belval, where two preserved blast furnaces stand over a university campus and a concert hall.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Prënzebierg-Giele Botter reserve above Differdange at dusk: former open-cast workings, now orchid meadows and red-rock cliffs, with the Titelberg Celtic oppidum on the next ridge. Drive into Luxembourg City for the last two nights.
itinerary.dayStats: 132 km · 2 h 30 drive · no passes · max altitude 420 m at Prënzebierg

itinerary.title: Fortress city, then home
itinerary.morning: Leave the car parked and walk: the Bock casemates, the Chemin de la Corniche above the Alzette, then the Pfaffenthal panoramic lift down into the Grund.
itinerary.afternoon: Kirchberg for the architecture, Mudam by I.M. Pei (2006) on the ramparts of Fort Thüngen, with the Philharmonie by Christian de Portzamparc (2005) alongside.
itinerary.evening: Return the car at Findel, fifteen minutes from Kirchberg. Fill the tank on the way; Luxembourg fuel is a parting gift.
itinerary.dayStats: 42 km · 55 min drive · no passes · max altitude 380 m on the Kirchberg plateau

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Belle-Vue
accommodationStrategy.description: On the Grand-Rue facing the castle rock, with its own parking, which matters, because Vianden's street bays fill by mid-afternoon in summer. Two nights here covers the Our valley, Mont Saint-Nicolas and Bourscheid with no repositioning.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Bel Air
accommodationStrategy.description: Parkland on the edge of town, secure off-street parking, and a garden that makes a good decompression stop between the Mullerthal lanes and the Moselle. Fifteen minutes' walk to the basilica.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2 months ahead for the Whit Tuesday procession.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hôtel Parc Beaux-Arts
accommodationStrategy.description: Three converted 18th-century houses on Rue Sigefroi, thirty seconds from the casemates. Book a parking space with the room; the old town is a maze of resident-only bays.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6 weeks; avoid EU summit weeks, when rates double.

logistics.emergency: 112 for ambulance and fire; 113 for police in Luxembourg. Coverage is near-universal, the deep Our and Sûre valleys are the only weak spots.
logistics.weather: The Oesling plateau at 500 m runs 5-8°C colder and considerably windier than the Moselle on the same day; fog on the N7 crest is common at dawn in autumn.
logistics.money: Cards are accepted almost everywhere, including small wineries, but a few village parking meters and rural bakeries still want coins. Tipping is rounding up, not a percentage.
logistics.transportRules: Use it for the Moselle wine day and the capital, where parking is the only real cost. Alcohol limit is 0.5 g/l, and 0.2 g/l for licences under two years old.

other.label: Tolls: there are none
other.text: Luxembourg charges nothing for any road, motorway included, and requires no vignette, nor do Belgium or Germany for cars. Budget zero for road charges.

other.label: Low-emission zones
other.text: Luxembourg has none. Brussels, Antwerp and Ghent all run LEZs that require foreign plates to be registered online in advance, and German cities with an *Umweltzone* need a Feinstaubplakette (approx. €6). Neither applies on this loop; both bite if you extend it.

other.label: Fuel strategy
other.text: Fill inside Luxembourg, always: the gap with neighbours is worth 15-25% on a tank. Border stations at Wasserbillig, Schengen, Dudelange and Martelange open late and take foreign cards.

other.label: Winter tyres are a legal requirement
other.text: in wintry conditions, not a recommendation. Rentals collected October-April should carry them; confirm at the desk.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Most museums and castles close Mondays; several Minett sites run weekends only outside July-August, and Sunday afternoons in small towns are genuinely shut.

other.label: Cross-border rental
other.text: Cars from Findel can be driven freely into Belgium, Germany and France, but one-way drops abroad typically add €150, €400, and the border is 20 km away in three directions.

proTips: Buy the **LuxembourgCard** (approx. €13, €28 per person per day, cheaper for multi-day) on the morning of the Minett day: the mine museum, Fond-de-Gras, Vianden château and Clervaux together beat its cost in one afternoon.
Vianden castle is quietest **before 10:30**, when the coach groups arrive from the Moselle river cruises.
On the Moselle, ask for **Auxerrois** rather than Riesling, it is what the growers drink here, rarely exported and priced accordingly.
**Park at P+R Bouillon** on the capital's south-west edge and ride the free tram in. It saves €20, €30 a day and skips the one-way system.
The **Schiessentümpel** has roadside parking for about a dozen cars. Arrive before 09:30 or leave the car in Berdorf and walk the extra 25 minutes.

packingNotes: Offline maps for the CR network; satnavs route you onto farm tracks between Bavigne and Boulaide.
A small stash of €2 coins for older village parking meters that still refuse cards.
Wind shell and warm mid-layer for the plateau, plus something lighter for the Moselle.
Grippy shoes for Mullerthal sandstone, which is slick after rain and often wet regardless.
A jacket for the Rumelange mine gallery, a constant 12°C.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Rain turns the Mullerthal into a sponge** and the sandstone paths hold water for days. Swap Day 4 and Day 5; the Moselle works in any weather.
**Industrial heritage runs on a weekend timetable.** Train 1900 and the Minièresbunn may not operate midweek or off-season. The Rumelange mine museum and Belval keep longer hours year-round.
**Vianden's parking saturates** on summer weekends and during the early-August medieval festival. Use the riverside lots by the campsite and walk up in ten minutes.

**Straying into a Belgian LEZ unregistered** brings an automatic fine by post plus the rental company's admin fee. Registering a foreign plate online is free, do it before any detour toward Antwerp or Brussels.
**The A7 tunnels close for maintenance** overnight and occasionally at weekends, diverting traffic onto the old road through Mersch. Allow an extra 25 minutes on airport days.
